correctness.rationale: Independence gives edge weight ℓq^(m−1) for a focal edge with m descendant tips. The common ancestral path cancels, and ultrametricity ensures the remaining coefficient sum is zero, so the difference factors as (q−1) times a sum of truncated geometric series. For at most six tips singleton splits have fixed sign and the other splits are (2,2), (2,3), (3,3) with degree at most one, or (4,2) with strictly positive derivative a₄(1+2q)+a₃. The new seven-tip splits (1,6), (2,5), (3,4) give fixed sign, monotonicity, and degree at most two respectively. Identical score polynomials and the tie at q=1 do not count. The witness is fully binary with positive lengths and all heights 4; its two marginal polynomials differ by (q−1)(q−3/10)(q−4/5). An independent enumeration of all 64 survivor subsets for each focal tip gives differences −63/500, 3/100, −3/500 at q=1/10, 1/2, 9/10. Attaching a new root above the old tree with one new sister tip adds the same tq^(n−1) to both scores, preserving both crossings.
residual_risks: No sharp bound for n>7 is established; persistence there is existence only. No machine-checked proof is claimed.

originality.rationale: Credit the exact ultrametric seven-tip onset for two sign reversals of a fixed HED pair. Expected marginal PD and its edge identity are known; the closest equivalent protection-gain formulation has a five-tip threshold without the ultrametric constraint. Its five-tip counterexample cannot decide the restricted threshold. No inspected result settles that precise restriction.
residual_risks: The thesis comparison remains incomplete. These statement-level comparisons do not exclude unindexed work or a mathematically equivalent result under another name.

checked_sources: Frozen Finding and proof, especially the small splits and seven-tip witness
value.rationale: The first possible repeated change of a fixed priority comparison is a meaningful robustness boundary for an established conservation score. Both the impossibility below the boundary and a rational tree attaining it matter. The comparison with the non-ultrametric five-tip threshold isolates the mathematical effect of imposing equal heights. This does not establish that such crossings are frequent in data or quantify the maximum for larger trees.
residual_risks: Conservation implications are confined to common independent risks and the fixed-tree conditional score.
